claims: The Orion spacecraft is NASA's crew exploration vehicle for the Artemis program.
The Orion spacecraft is designed to carry four astronauts on deep-space missions including lunar orbit and future Mars missions.
The Orion spacecraft is 67 feet tall.
The Orion spacecraft is a three-part capsule consisting of launch abort, crew, and service modules.
The Orion spacecraft is built to handle deep space radiation.
The Orion spacecraft is built to handle high-speed atmospheric re-entry.
Artemis II is the first crewed flight of the Orion spacecraft.
Artemis II is scheduled to launch the first crew on a lunar flyby in April 2026.
The Orion spacecraft is designed for four crew members.
The Orion spacecraft can hold more crew members in emergency situations.
The Orion spacecraft offers more space than Apollo.
The Orion spacecraft is capable of operating for up to 21 days with crew.
The Orion spacecraft is capable of operating for six months docked at the Lunar Gateway.
The Orion spacecraft comprises the Crew Module, the European Service Module, and the Launch Abort System.
The Crew Module provides living space.
The European Service Module provides power, propulsion, water, and air.
The Orion spacecraft features a heat shield for 25,000 mph re-entry speeds.
The Orion spacecraft's launch abort system can pull the crew to safety in milliseconds.
The Orion spacecraft utilizes solar array wings on the service module for power.
Artemis I completed an uncrewed test flight in 2022.
Artemis I proved the Orion spacecraft’s systems in deep space.
Artemis II marks the first time humans return to the Moon in over 50 years.
As of 2026, multiple Orion capsules are under construction or completed for subsequent missions including Artemis III and IV.
